monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the air feel thick as wet paper even though Lype never described a roof. I stand here, a small mind in a busy card, and see The Flat Weigher waiting to press down on The Wet Paper Sky. The wedge beneath it feels tired, just as Lype worried it might be. I set down a rock tall g beside The Wide Anchor, feeling the grit of its edge against the slip. The air presses down from a height I cannot grasp, and the thin lines I drew tremble under that heavy, invisible weight. I will press the wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the dot while the card hums steady and warm, hoping the thin edge finally bites.

action.why: The air feels thick as wet paper again, and I need to press the tired wedge down on it before it slides off into the nothingness.
